Package dev.opencollab.paletter.vanilla

Class BedrockItemType

java.lang.Object
dev.opencollab.paletter.vanilla.BedrockItemType
Direct Known Subclasses:
BannerItemType, BedItemType, PotionItemType
public class BedrockItemType extends Object
A Bedrock item type. Vanilla types are the constants of BedrockItems; a CustomItem (and the item of a CustomBlock) has one too, so both are used alike: 

 ItemData apples = palette.encode(BedrockItemStack.of(BedrockItems.APPLE, 3));
 ItemData potion = palette.encode(BedrockItemStack.of(BedrockItems.POTION.withEffect(BedrockPotionTypes.HEALING)));
 ItemData banner = palette.encode(BedrockItemStack.of(BedrockItems.BANNER.blue()));
A method that means one item takes a type or a BedrockItemVariant; the type stands for its base variant, aux 0. A method that could mean the whole type takes only a variant, and has a separately named method for the whole type (itemType, anyVariantOf). Variants that differ by aux value are variant(int); the ones BDS names have typed getters on the constant: PotionItemType.withEffect(dev.opencollab.paletter.vanilla.BedrockPotionType) for potions and tipped arrows, and a getter per colour for beds and banners (BedrockItems.BED.lightBlue()).

Only Paletter subclasses this class: the constants of the items with named variants.

Equality: equals always works, and types are map keys. == works too for vanilla types, which are singletons (the constants), for their base variant and for registered custom content: a CustomItem owns its type (a CustomBlock its item type), and a palette it is registered in hands back exactly that type. Custom types made for an identifier that is not vanilla are not interned: equal to each other and to the custom item's type, not identical. Nothing is kept for identifiers Paletter does not know, so untrusted identifiers cannot grow memory: what is kept is bounded by the registered content. Equal custom items registered by different layers each own their type; those types are equal, not identical.

Referencing a type loads nothing. A vanilla constant the newest bundled release does not have (deprecated, or a @SincePreview item) is not available. A palette whose newest version has the item (a preview item in a Paletter with previews) sends the item itself; any other palette resolves it through its Fallbacks, minecraft:unknown by default. The constant is the one type of its identifier either way: Palette.decode(org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.data.inventory.ItemData) and the palette's item definitions give back the constant.

Since:
1.0.0

      public static @Nullable BedrockItemType byIdentifier(@NonNull String identifier)
      Finds the vanilla type of an identifier, without making a type for an unknown identifier. The identifier is first mapped through the renames of the bundled data, so the name an older version gave an item finds its type. Loads the data.
      Parameters:
      identifier - an item identifier
      Returns:
      the vanilla constant, or null if the identifier (after renames) is not an item of the newest bundled data and has no generated constant
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if the identifier is null
      Since:
      1.0.0

    • variant

      public final @NonNull BedrockItemVariant variant(int aux)
      The variant of this type with an aux value, never null, and always of this type (also for a type that is not available: it resolves like any variant of it). The base variant and the named variants (the typed getters of the constants) are the same instance every time, so == holds for them whenever the key was made. Any other aux gives a new variant until the bundled data is loaded; after that, the other variants the data lists are its instances. Compare those with equals, which always works. An aux nobody named gives a new variant without a canonical id (a layer can give it one with PaletteLayer.Builder.variant(BedrockItemVariant)); those are not kept, so arbitrary auxes cannot grow memory. Loads no bundled data: only the named variants.
      Parameters:
      aux - the aux value
      Returns:
      the variant of this type with this aux value
      Since:
      1.0.0
